st.3: Lothal lies on the Narmada near the Gulf of Khambhat.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Lothal lies on the Bhogava, near its confluence with the Sabarmati, not on the Narmada.

st.2: Lothal had bead-making workshops.

x: Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4 are correct: Rakhigarhi had a gemstone factory, Lothal had bead workshops, and Chanhudaro, the only Harappan city without a citadel, had bead-making and shell-ornament factories.
All three statements are correct: Santamula I gave away crores of gold coins, kahapana and nikkha first appear clearly in Pali texts, and the Mada was a gold coin of the Kakatiyas.

st.3: Chariot racing was a popular pastime.

x: All three statements are correct: sura was the intoxicating drink and soma the ritual drink, the gambler's hymn is Rigveda X.34, and chariot racing was a favourite pastime of the Rigvedic people.

st.3: Yava (barley) was the chief crop of the Rigvedic period.

x: All three statements are correct: vrihi (rice) and godhuma (wheat) appear only in later Vedic texts, while yava (barley) was the chief Rigvedic crop.

st.1: Adi Shankaracharya founded four mathas, one of them at Udupi.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Shankara's four mathas are at Sringeri, Dwaraka, Puri and Jyotirmath; Udupi is associated with Madhvacharya.

st.3: Rudradaman I repaired it without forced labour.

x: All four statements are correct: Pushyagupta built the lake, Tushaspha added canals, Rudradaman I repaired it without forced labour (Junagadh inscription), and Skandagupta repaired it again.

st.3: Danda (the army) is the sixth standard element, just before Mitra.

x: All three statements are correct: the seven elements run Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda and Mitra, so Danda is sixth and the ally (Mitra) last; Shatru is not one of them.

st.2: The Amaravati stupa stands on the right bank of the Krishna.

x: All three statements are correct: the Mallas built the Ranabhar stupa, the Amaravati stupa is on the right bank of the Krishna, and Bhattiprolu has the oldest stupa of Andhra.

st.2: The Huna ruler Toramana persecuted Buddhism.
st.3: The Kahaum pillar of Skandagupta's time records a Sun temple.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it was Toramana's son Mihirakula who persecuted Buddhism. Statement 3 is wrong: the Kahaum pillar records Jain images, not a Sun temple.

st.3: In April 2025 the Prime Minister gifted a Sarnath-style Buddha in Bhumisparsha mudra to the King of Thailand.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Sarnath-style Buddha gifted in April 2025 was in Dhyan mudra, not Bhumisparsha mudra.

st.3: They were rediscovered in 1819 by John Smith, a British officer on a tiger hunt.

x: All four statements are correct: Ajanta is in Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) district, five of its 30 caves are chaityas, John Smith rediscovered it in 1819, and it became a UNESCO site in 1983.

st.3: Bhaskara I wrote a commentary on the Brahmasphutasiddhanta.
st.4: The Gwalior inscription of 876 CE shows zero as a dot.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Bhaskara I wrote a commentary on the Aryabhatiya. Statement 4 is wrong: the Gwalior inscription (876 CE) shows zero as a small circle.

st.2: The Aihole inscription that records it belongs to 634 CE.
st.4: After the conflict Harsha accepted the Godavari as his southern border.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Pulakesin II stopped Harsha on the Narmada, the Aihole inscription is of 634 CE, and he took the title Dakshinapatheshwara. Statement 4 is wrong: Harsha accepted the Narmada, not the Godavari, as his southern border.

st.3: Rajamahendravaram was first made the capital by Rajaraja Narendra.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Rajamahendravaram was first made the capital by the Eastern Chalukya Amma I; Rajaraja Narendra only made it famous.

st.3: Burton Stein described the Chola state as segmentary.

x: All three statements are correct: the Chola empire had eight mandalams, each under a viceroy, and Burton Stein called the Chola state segmentary, not centralised.

st.1: Ghari was a grazing tax on milch cattle.
st.2: Charai was a house tax.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statements 1 and 2 swap the terms: ghari was the house tax and charai the grazing tax on milch cattle.

st.2: Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498 during the reign of Ibrahim Lodi.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Vasco da Gama arrived in 1498 during the reign of Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517), not Ibrahim Lodi.

st.2: The social liberation theory explains conversions only partially, as caste-like ranks survived among converts.

x: Both statements are correct: political patronage and social liberation are each only partial explanations, since caste-like ranks persisted among converts.

st.2: In 1535, pressed by Humayun, Bahadur Shah of Gujarat let the Portuguese fortify Daman.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: pressed by Humayun, Bahadur Shah let the Portuguese build a fort at Diu, not Daman.

st.3: Akbar wrote an autobiography in Turki.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it was Babur who wrote his autobiography (Tuzuk-i-Baburi) in Turki; Akbar wrote none.

st.2: Each revenue circle was to yield one crore tankas.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: each circle was to yield one crore dams (the Mughal copper coin), not tankas.

st.2: The Peacock Throne made for him was carried away by Nadir Shah.

x: All three statements are correct: Shah Jahan was crowned at Agra in 1628, Nadir Shah carried off the Peacock Throne in 1739, and Jujhar Singh and Khan Jahan Lodi revolted early in his reign.

st.1: 'Mansab' is an Arabic word meaning rank.

x: All four statements are correct: mansab is an Arabic word for rank, Abul Fazl lists 66 grades with 33 in practice, ranks ran from 10 to 10,000, and civil officials were also mansabdars.

st.2: The shroffs issued hundis.

x: All three statements are correct: bima insured goods in transit, shroffs issued hundis (bills of exchange), and Multanis and Khurasanis dominated Sultanate overseas trade.

st.3: The Chettis dominated the Malabar coast and Muslim merchants the Coromandel coast.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 swaps the coasts: the Chettis dominated the Coromandel coast and Muslim (Mappila) merchants the Malabar coast.

st.2: Jodha Bai's palace is one of the palaces of Fatehpur Sikri.

x: All three statements are correct: Salim Chishti's tomb is in the Jama Masjid courtyard, Jodha Bai's palace is the largest palace of Fatehpur Sikri, and the Tudor arch continued at Orchha. (The Akbari Mahal is in Agra Fort.)

st.3: The Charyapada, whose manuscript Haraprasad Shastri found in the Nepal royal library, are songs of Buddhist Siddhacharyas.

x: All three statements are correct: Matsyendranath and Gorakhnath led the Nathpanthis, who practised hatha yoga and were open to 'low' castes, and the Charyapada are songs of Buddhist Siddhacharyas.

st.3: The Anubhava Mantapa, the assembly of sharanas, was presided over by Allama Prabhu.

x: All four statements are correct: Basavanna was born at Bagewadi and served Bijjala at Kalyana, Allama Prabhu presided over the Anubhava Mantapa, and Akkamahadevi was a leading sharana.

st.4: He inspired Palnati Brahmanaidu's Veera Vaishnava movement.

x: All four statements are correct: Velanati Cholas and Palnati Haihayas patronised Sri Vaishnavism, Ramanuja installed Govindaraja at Tirupati, gave Panchamas temple entry and inspired Brahmanaidu's Veera Vaishnava movement.

st.3: Vyasa Tirtha was a scholar of the Dvaita (Madhva) school.

x: All three statements are correct: Vallabhacharya defeated Vyasa Tirtha in debate at Krishnadevaraya's court, Vyasa Tirtha was Rajaguru of Saluva Narasimha and Krishnadevaraya, and he belonged to the Dvaita school.

st.2: He abandoned Almeida's Blue Water Policy.

x: All three statements are correct: Albuquerque took Goa from Bijapur in 1510, gave up Almeida's Blue Water Policy for a land empire, and abolished sati in his territories.

st.2: Chandernagore, settled with the permission of Shaista Khan, lies on the Hooghly in Bengal.
st.4: Mahe, a French settlement of 1725, lies on the Coromandel coast.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Sher Khan Lodi gave the Pondicherry land, Chandernagore is on the Hooghly in Bengal, and Fort St. Louis was the French headquarters. Statement 4 is wrong: Mahe lies on the Malabar coast.

st.3: Scindia was the last Maratha power to accept it, in 1818.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the last Maratha power to accept it was Holkar (1818), not Scindia.

st.1: The Inam Commission of 1852 was set up in the Bombay Presidency.

x: All three statements are correct: the Inam Commission (1852) worked in the Bombay Presidency, the lower courts favoured the rich while Indians were kept out of high posts, and the drain meant the transfer of resources to Britain.

st.3: The Council of India was set up to advise the Governor-General.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 15-member Council of India advised the Secretary of State, not the Governor-General.

st.2: Chanda Sahib had been released from Maratha captivity.
st.4: In the Carnatic the English backed Chanda Sahib.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Nizam-ul-Mulk died in 1748, Chanda Sahib was released by the Marathas, and Muzaffar Jang was the Nizam's daughter's son. Statement 4 is wrong: the English backed Muhammad Ali; the French backed Chanda Sahib.

st.1: The Tripartite Treaty of 1838 is associated with Lord Auckland.

x: All three statements are correct: the Tripartite Treaty (1838) was Lord Auckland's, Ochterlony forced terms on Nepal after Almora, and Yandabo (1826) gave Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim.

st.2: It was subdued by Warren Hastings.

x: All three statements are correct: the Sanyasi revolt lasted from 1763 to 1800, was subdued by Warren Hastings, and was led by Majnum Shah and Bhawani Pathak.

st.2: The Bhonsle of Berar accepted it after the Peshwa.

x: All three statements are correct: Baji Rao II signed the Treaty of Bassein in December 1802, the Bhonsle accepted it only after the Second Anglo-Maratha War (Deogaon, 1803), and Holkar was last, in 1818.
Both statements are correct: the 1879-80 Rampa rebellion was led by Agency leaders such as Chandrayya and Ambul Reddy, and the 1922-24 rebellion by Alluri Sitarama Raju.

st.4: Kandukuri Veeresalingam started Hasyasanjivani in 1876.

x: All four statements are correct: Telugu journalism dates from 1835, Andhra Prakasika (1885) was the first political weekly, and Veeresalingam started Vivekavardhini (1874) and Hasyasanjivani (1876).

st.2: The League's session was presided over by M.A. Jinnah.
st.3: Tilak's group was readmitted to the Congress at the Calcutta session.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: both bodies met at Lucknow, Jinnah presided over the League session, and it was Gandhi's first session after South Africa. Statement 3 is wrong: Tilak's group was readmitted at the Lucknow session of 1916.

st.3: Annamalai University was founded in 1929.

x: All four statements are correct: the Communal G.O. (1921) gave non-Brahmins a share, Madras first let women vote (1921), Annamalai University came in 1929, and Andhra University began at Bezawada before moving to Waltair.

st.2: The Deva Samaj of Lahore (1887) was founded by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri.

x: All three statements are correct: Ramabai Ranade and G.K. Devadhar founded the Poona Seva Sadan, Shiv Narayan Agnihotri the Deva Samaj, and Krishnarao Bhalekar ran Din Bandhu.

st.3: He embraced Buddhism at Yeola on 14 October 1956.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Ambedkar embraced Buddhism at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur; Yeola is where he made his 1935 declaration.

st.3: Its aggressive campaign of the 1920s was led by Swami Shraddhanand.

x: All four statements are correct: Shuddhi sought reconversion and the uplift of untouchables, its 1920s campaign was led by Swami Shraddhanand, and it sharpened communalism.
All three statements are correct: the Singh Sabha promoted Gurmukhi and education, removed un-Sikh practices, and the Akali movement grew out of it.

st.3: The foundation stone of the Khalsa College, Amritsar was laid in 1892.

x: All three statements are correct: the first Singh Sabha was founded at Amritsar (1873), the Lahore Sabha in 1879, and the Khalsa College stone was laid in 1892.

st.2: Muhammad Iqbal proposed a North-West Indian Muslim state at the Lahore session of the Muslim League in 1930.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Iqbal proposed the North-West Muslim state at the Allahabad session of 1930, not at Lahore.

st.2: Congressmen boycotted the November 1920 legislative elections.

x: All three statements are correct: courts were to give way to panchayats with khadi promoted, the Congress boycotted the November 1920 council elections (council entry came later with the Swarajists), and the Tilak Swaraj Fund was oversubscribed.

st.3: It reserved seats for the depressed classes only in the provincial legislatures, not in the Central Legislature.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Poona Pact also reserved 18 per cent of the general seats in the Central Legislature for the depressed classes.

st.2: It was started by Vinoba Bhave at Sabarmati Ashram.
st.3: Its aim was mass mobilisation to paralyse the British war effort.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Vinoba Bhave began it at Paunar near Wardha. Statement 3 is wrong: it was deliberately limited and symbolic, meant to assert free speech without hampering the war effort.

st.2: Gandhi's Quit India writings appeared in Young India.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Gandhi's Quit India writings appeared in Harijan, not Young India.

st.1: He founded the Andhra Bank at Vijayawada in 1923.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Pattabhi founded the Andhra Bank at Machilipatnam, not Vijayawada.

st.4: The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873) was founded by Jyotiba Phule.

st.3: Pattabhi Sitaramayya lost the Congress presidential contest to Subhas Bose at Haripura in 1938.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Bose was elected unopposed at Haripura (1938); Pattabhi lost to him in the contest for the Tripuri session (1939).

st.3: The title 'Socrates of Maharashtra' belongs to Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 'Socrates of Maharashtra' was Gopal Krishna Gokhale, not Tilak.

st.2: K.V. Reddy Naidu's proposal to name it 'Telugu University' was defeated.

x: All three statements are correct: M. Suryanarayana moved the 1921 resolution, Reddy Naidu's 'Telugu University' name was voted down, and A.P. Patro introduced C.R. Reddy's Bill on 20 August 1925.

st.1: The New Rayalaseema Mahasabha of 1938 held its first session at Adoni.

x: All three statements are correct: the New Rayalaseema Mahasabha (1938) first met at Adoni, the Madras session (1934) under Nemali Pattabhirama Rao asked for a university at Tirupati, and the Kadapa session (1935) opposed a separate Andhra.

st.2: Nehru promised a committee during his 1948 visit to Visakhapatnam.

x: All three statements are correct: Andhra was left out of the Draft Constitution (21 February 1948), Nehru promised a committee at Visakhapatnam in 1948, and the Centre feared for national unity.

st.3: The animal most commonly painted there is the deer.

x: All four statements are correct: Bhimbetka is in Raisen district (UNESCO 2003), about 300 shelters have Upper Palaeolithic art, the deer is the most painted animal, and the 2026 study found the style became static after Chalcolithic contact.

st.2: Gautami Balasri's Nasik inscription was issued in the reign of her grandson Vasishthiputra Pulumavi.

x: All three statements are correct: Naganika's Naneghat record lists sacrifices and gifts, Gautami Balasri's Nasik inscription dates from Pulumavi's reign, not Gautamiputra's, and Pulumavi II's Amaravati inscription is the first Satavahana record in Andhra.

st.2: Kondapur, a fortified Satavahana town known for terracotta, beads and coins, is in Khammam district.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kondapur is in Sangareddy (old Medak) district, not Khammam.

st.3: It was excavated by Alexander Rea in 1892.

x: All three statements are correct: Bhattiprolu is the oldest stupa of AP, its caskets name Raja Kubiraka and the Nigama Sabha, and Alexander Rea excavated it in 1892 (Burgess excavated Jaggayyapeta).

st.2: Its main medium was blue-grey schist.

x: Both statements are correct: Gandhara art flourished around Peshawar, Taxila and Swat, and used blue-grey schist (and stucco); spotted red sandstone was the Mathura medium.

st.3: The Kopparam plates (631) of Pulakeshin II call Kubja Vishnuvardhana 'Maharaja'.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Kopparam plates call Kubja Vishnuvardhana 'Yuvaraja', not 'Maharaja'.

st.2: The Pasupata sect was the peaceful one, while the Kalamukhas were extremists.

x: All three statements are correct: the Pasupata sect of Lakulisha was the oldest and the peaceful one, the Kalamukhas were the extremists, and Draksharama, Kaleshwaram and Srisailam formed the Trilinga desa.

st.2: The Maliyapundi grant to the Jinalaya at Dharmavaram was made at the request of the vassal Durgaraja.

x: All three statements are correct: the Kaluchumbarru grant was made at Chamekamba's request, the Maliyapundi grant at the request of Durgaraja, and Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave for Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva.

st.2: Under it sons acquire a right in ancestral property only on the father's death.

x: All three statements are correct: Jimutavahana wrote the Dayabhaga, under which sons get a right only after the father's death (unlike the Mitakshara's right by birth), and it prevails in Bengal and Assam.

st.3: The gold tax was abolished by Anavota Reddi.
st.4: Meruka was a house tax.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Bhumi Sistu was the main income, temple, Brahmin and Ayagar lands were exempt, and Anavota Reddi abolished the gold tax. Statement 4 is wrong: Meruka was a tax on wetlands; the house tax was Illari.
Both statements are correct: Gulbarga, the first Bahmani capital, was renamed Hasanabad, and Ahmad Shah I moved the capital to Bidar.
Both statements are correct: the Dutch set up a factory at Machilipatnam in 1605, and Captain Hippon reached it in the Globe in 1611 for the English.

st.2: 'Prabandha Parameshwara' was the title of Errana.

x: All three statements are correct: Krishnadevaraya fixed the Gandapenderam on Peddana's foot, 'Prabandha Parameshwara' was Errana's title (not Nandi Timmana's), and Peddana was 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha'.

st.1: It does not record a genealogy of the dynasty from Bukka to Krishnadevaraya.

x: All three statements are correct: Amuktamalyada gives no genealogy from Bukka (the Tuluvas did not descend from him), but it refers to Krishnadevaraya's campaigns and discusses rajaniti.

st.2: The Bhandara department looked after the treasury.

x: All three statements are correct: the Rayavachakam lists nine departments under Sampratis, the Bhandara was the treasury (Athavane was revenue), and the Dharmasana was judicial.

st.2: Of Prataparudra's 75 generals, only three survived.

x: All three statements are correct: Warangal became Sultanpur under Malik Burhanuddin and Malik Maqbul, only three of the 75 generals survived (Prolaya Nayaka, Recherla Singama, Prolaya Vema Reddi), and the Vimochanodyamam was the first organised resistance.

st.3: He was the second holder of the title Andhra Suratrana, after Prolaya Nayaka.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kapaya Nayaka was the first holder of the title Andhra Suratrana.

st.3: The steps to Tirumala are credited to Anantaraju.

x: All three statements are correct: the Srisailam mukha mandapam is Harihara II's, the prakaram Shanti Lingayya's, and the steps to Tirumala Anantaraju's (Krishnadevaraya gave the kalyana mandapam and bronzes).

st.3: Anavota Reddi lifted customs duties there.

x: All four statements are correct: Marco Polo came in 1287 under Rudrama Devi, Ganapatideva and the minister Somaya issued Abhaya Sasanas, and Anavota Reddi lifted customs duties.

st.1: Public loyalty meetings for the British were held at Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Machilipatnam.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the loyalty meetings were at Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, not Machilipatnam.

st.4: Arthur Cotton was knighted in 1861.

x: All four statements are correct: the Bezwada anicut is today's Prakasam Barrage, the Sangam anicut is on the Penna, the deltas are the 'Rice Bowl of Andhra', and Cotton was knighted in 1861.

st.2: Andhra Patrika was first published from Bombay on 9 September 1908.

x: All four statements are correct: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded and edited Andhra Patrika, which began in Bombay in 1908 and became a daily in 1914, and Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty founded The Crescent.

st.1: He showed his 1921 tricolour design to Gandhi at the Bezwada AICC session, and Gandhi added the Ashoka Chakra.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: at Bezwada (1921) Gandhi asked for the spinning wheel (charkha) to be added; the Ashoka Chakra came only in 1947.

st.1: The Objectives Resolution was moved by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Objectives Resolution was moved by Nehru on 13 December 1946 (adopted 22 January 1947).

st.1: Porus was reinstated as ruler after his defeat at the Hydaspes.

x: All three statements are correct: Alexander restored Porus to his kingdom, founded Bucephala and Nicaea on the Jhelum, and killed Astes of Pushkalavati who resisted him.

st.2: It was the first Buddhist council held in Sanskrit.

x: All three statements are correct: the Fourth Council met at Kundalavana in Kashmir, used Sanskrit (not Pali), and Vasumitra compiled the Mahavibhasha there.

st.3: Kovalan, wrongly accused of stealing the queen's anklet, is executed by the Pandya king.

x: All four statements are correct: Ilango Adigal was Senguttuvan's brother and, by tradition, Karikala's grandson; the Pandya king (not the Chola) executes Kovalan; and Kannagi burns Madurai.

st.3: Valabhi was a Mahayana centre of Harsha's time under the Maitrakas.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Valabhi under the Maitrakas was a Hinayana centre; Nalanda was the Mahayana one.

st.3: They lie near the Tapti river.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Ellora lies near Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), far from the Tapti.

st.2: The Hindu caves (13-29) were mainly carved by the Rashtrakutas.

x: All three statements are correct: the Buddhist caves are the earliest, the Hindu caves were mainly Rashtrakuta work, and the Kailasa is the latest of the four named.

st.2: The Hoysaleswara temple at Halebid, built c. 1121 by Ketamalla, an officer of Vishnuvardhana, is dedicated to Shiva.

x: All three statements are correct: Vishnuvardhana built the Chennakeshava at Belur (1117), Ketamalla's Hoysaleswara at Halebid is a Shiva temple, and Somanatha built the Keshava temple at Somanathapura (1268).

st.1: The Economic Survey 2025-26 lists land inheritance as a driver of social mobility.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Survey names health, education, technology and institutions as drivers of mobility, not land inheritance.

st.3: The PMEGP is implemented by NABARD.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the PMEGP is implemented by the KVIC, not NABARD.

st.2: Military expenditure is one of the dimensions of the WEF Global Gender Gap Index.
st.4: The Women, Peace and Security Index 2023 is published by the World Economic Forum.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Gender Gap Index covers economy, education, health and politics, not military spending. Statement 4 is wrong: the WPS Index is published by the Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace and Security with PRIO.

st.3: The JJ Act 2015 allows 16-18-year-olds to be tried as adults for all offences.
st.4: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita was enacted as a direct outcome of the case.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 16-18-year-olds may be tried as adults only for heinous offences. Statement 4 is wrong: the direct outcome was the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, not the BNS.

Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Convention 138 sets the minimum age, Convention 182 covers the worst forms of child labour, and the World Day is on 12 June. Statement 3 is wrong: India ratified both conventions on 13 June 2017, not in 2007.

st.2: ASEAN observed 1990 as the Year of the Girl Child.
st.3: CBSE Udaan aims to increase the enrolment of girls in premier medical colleges.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 1990 was the SAARC (not ASEAN) Year of the Girl Child. Statement 3 is wrong: Udaan targets premier engineering institutions, not medical colleges.

st.1: YSR Aasara covers the crop loans of farmers outstanding on 11 April 2019.
st.3: The Disha Bill, 2019 became law after receiving Presidential assent.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: YSR Aasara covers SHG loans, not farmers' crop loans. Statement 3 is wrong: the Disha Bill never received Presidential assent.

st.1: It was launched on 8 March 2018 at Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on 8 March 2018 at Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan.

All three statements are correct: invalidity and old age pensions are Concurrent List Entry 24, the NSAP rests on Articles 41 and 42, and Himachal Pradesh passed the first State maintenance law in 2001.

st.1: PM-KISAN gives only small and marginal landholding farmers ₹6,000 a year in 3 instalments.
st.2: PM-KISAN is a Centrally Sponsored scheme with a 60:40 Centre-State share.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: since 2019 PM-KISAN covers all landholding farmer families, not only small and marginal ones. Statement 2 is wrong: it is a Central Sector scheme fully funded by the Centre.

st.2: MEPMA covers 2.74 lakh rural SHGs.
st.3: Streenidhi is a scheduled commercial bank (2011) giving SHG members quick loans.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: MEPMA works with urban SHGs (2.74 lakh), not rural ones. Statement 3 is wrong: Streenidhi is a credit cooperative, not a commercial bank.

st.1: Special education targets gifted children.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: special education targets children with disabilities, not gifted children.

st.1: Katchatheevu was ceded by India to Sri Lanka under an agreement signed by Rajiv Gandhi.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Katchatheevu was ceded under the 1974 agreement between Indira Gandhi and Sirimavo Bandaranaike.

st.2: The Punatsangchhu hydroelectric projects are located in Nepal.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Punatsangchhu projects are in Bhutan, not Nepal.
All three statements are correct: India-GCC trade is over $160 billion, the first I2U2 leaders' summit was virtual in 2022, and MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division handles I2U2.

st.1: The United States designated India a 'Major Non-NATO Ally'.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: India is a 'Major Defense Partner' (2016) of the US, not a Major Non-NATO Ally.

st.3: Kovvada, the proposed site for Westinghouse AP1000 reactors, is in Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kovvada is in Srikakulam district, not Nellore.

st.1: Khalilur Rahman of Pakistan is President of the 81st UN General Assembly (2026-27).

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Khalilur Rahman, President of the 81st UNGA, is from Bangladesh, not Pakistan.

st.3: The post-Hudhud Andhra Pradesh Disaster Recovery Project is funded by the ADB.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the post-Hudhud recovery project is funded by the World Bank, not the ADB.

st.3: The African Union replaced the OAU in 2002 and is headquartered at Nairobi.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the African Union is headquartered at Addis Ababa, not Nairobi.

st.1: It was launched on 10 November 2000 at Phnom Penh.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Mekong Ganga Cooperation was launched at Vientiane (Laos), not Phnom Penh.

st.3: India is a member of the OECD.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India is not a member of the OECD; it is only a key partner.

st.3: The revised Brisbane-eThekwini Goal was adopted at the G20 New Delhi Summit (2023).

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the revised Brisbane-eThekwini Goal (cut the labour-participation gap by 25% by 2030) came from the G20 Development Ministers in 2025 under South Africa.

st.2: The Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), responsible for external intelligence, works under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: RAW (1968) works under the Cabinet Secretariat, not the Home Ministry.
All three statements are correct: the Greyhounds are AP's anti-LWE force, they cut Naxal activity in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam districts, and they broke the red corridors on the AOB.

st.1: The Right to Property is now a Fundamental Right under Article 300A.
st.3: The local (third) tier of government was added by the 42nd Amendment.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: under Article 300A property is a constitutional (legal) right, not a Fundamental Right. Statement 3 is wrong: the third tier was added by the 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992).

st.1: It was based on the Nehru Report, the Round Table Conferences and the White Paper of 1933.
st.3: It gave residuary powers to the Provincial Legislatures.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Act was based on the Simon Commission report, not the Nehru Report. Statement 3 is wrong: residuary powers were vested in the Governor-General.

st.1: With the lapse of paramountcy, about 565 princely States automatically became part of India.
st.3: Hyderabad signed the Instrument of Accession in November 1947.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: on the lapse of paramountcy the States became theoretically free; they had to accede. Statement 3 is wrong: in November 1947 Hyderabad signed only a Standstill Agreement; it acceded after Operation Polo (1948).

st.1: The joint sitting of both Houses, borrowed from Australia, is presided over by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
st.3: If a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject clash, the State law always prevails.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the joint sitting is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. Statement 3 is wrong: the Union law prevails, unless a reserved State law gets the President's assent (Article 254).

st.1: In 2022, the Kerala High Court held that wearing the hijab is not an essential religious practice.
st.3: Haryana's Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act (2026) provides punishment for sacrilege.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 2022 hijab ruling was by the Karnataka High Court. Statement 3 is wrong: the Jaagat Jot Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026 is a Punjab law (up to life imprisonment for sacrilege).

st.3: The suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency is borrowed from the Constitution of the USA.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency is borrowed from the Weimar Constitution of Germany.

st.2: Liberty of action
st.4: Liberty of conscience

x: Items 1 and 3 are in the Preamble (liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; dignity of the individual). Liberty of action and liberty of conscience are not mentioned (conscience appears in Article 25).

st.1: It was introduced in Parliament as the 93rd Amendment Bill by the UPA government.
st.4: It deleted the Right to Property from the Fundamental Rights.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 93rd Amendment Bill was brought by the NDA government in 2001. Statement 4 is wrong: the Right to Property was deleted by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

st.1: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) upheld Parliament's unlimited power to amend the Constitution.
st.4: 'A right without a remedy is a worthless declaration' explains the importance of Article 21.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Kesavananda Bharati limited the amending power by the basic structure. Statement 4 is wrong: the maxim explains Article 32, the right to constitutional remedies.

st.2: It excluded the creamy layer among SCs and STs from reservation.
st.3: It removed the 50% ceiling on reservations.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Indra Sawhney applied the creamy-layer exclusion to the OBCs, not to SCs and STs. Statement 3 is wrong: it upheld the 50% ceiling.

st.4: It inserted Article 51A(k) as the first Fundamental Duty in the Constitution.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976); 51A(k) is the eleventh duty. (Article 39(f) too was reworded by the 42nd Amendment, not the 86th.)

st.1: Article 43A provides for participation of workers in the management of agriculture.
st.2: Article 48A provides for the separation of the judiciary from the executive.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 43A is about workers in the management of industries. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 48A is about the environment; separation of the judiciary is Article 50.

st.1: The Governor may return a Money Bill to the Legislature for reconsideration.
st.3: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council can reject a Money Bill within 14 days.
st.4: The Supreme Court's November 2025 advisory opinion held that courts can declare deemed assent.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: a Money Bill cannot be returned for reconsideration. Statement 3 is wrong: the Council cannot reject a Money Bill; it can only recommend within 14 days. Statement 4 is wrong: the opinion held that courts cannot declare deemed assent.

st.3: A Bill passed by both Houses and pending the President's assent lapses.
st.4: A Bill returned by the President for reconsideration lapses.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statements 3 and 4 are wrong: a Bill pending the President's assent, or returned by him for reconsideration, does not lapse on dissolution.

st.2: The Supreme Court has laid down an exhaustive list of the basic features.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Court has never given an exhaustive list; basic features are identified case by case.

st.2: Parliamentary Secretaries are members of the Council of Ministers, ranking just below Deputy Ministers.
st.3: The word 'Cabinet' was inserted into Article 352(3) by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Parliamentary Secretaries are not members of the Council of Ministers. Statement 3 is wrong: 'Cabinet' entered Article 352(3) through the 44th Amendment, 1978.

st.2: Sumitra Mahajan was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
st.3: G.V. Mavalankar is the only Lok Sabha Speaker who became President of India.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the first woman Speaker was Meira Kumar (2009). Statement 3 is wrong: N. Sanjiva Reddy, not Mavalankar, is the only Speaker who became President.

st.1: It was first set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1935.
st.3: The appointment of an Opposition member as its Chairman since 1967 is mandated by the Rules of Procedure of the Lok Sabha.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the PAC was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919. Statement 3 is wrong: an Opposition chairman is only a convention since 1967, not a rule.

st.2: The office of the LoP is provided for in the Constitution.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the LoP is a statutory office (1977 Act), not a constitutional one.

st.2: The Committee on Public Undertakings has replaced the Estimates Committee.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Committee on Public Undertakings works alongside the Estimates Committee; it has not replaced it.

st.3: It prohibits en-bloc (bulk) defections carried out through a merger.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the law permits a merger backed by two-thirds of the legislature party, which is why it is criticised.

st.1: The disqualification petitions against 23 YSRCP MLAs who moved to the TDP during 2014-19 were decided within three months.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the petitions against the 23 YSRCP MLAs were never decided during that Assembly's term.

st.3: The NJAC was to be chaired by the Union Law Minister.
st.4: The Attorney-General was one of its six members.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the NJAC was to be chaired by the Chief Justice of India; the Law Minister was a member. Statement 4 is wrong: the Attorney-General was not a member.

st.2: Under Article 323A, tribunals for public service matters can be set up by Parliament and State Legislatures.
st.3: Under Article 323B, tribunals for taxation, land reforms and rent can be set up only by Parliament.
st.4: Public service matters are among the subjects of Article 323B.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 323A tribunals can be set up only by Parliament. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 323B tribunals can be set up by both Parliament and the State Legislatures. Statement 4 is wrong: public service matters fall under Article 323A.

st.1: During a National Emergency, the Union may give directions to a State only on Union List matters.
st.2: During a National Emergency, the State governments are suspended.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Union may give directions to a State on any matter, not only Union List matters. Statement 2 is wrong: State governments continue; they are not suspended.

st.3: Disaster funds are shared 90:10 for all the States.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 90:10 sharing is only for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States; others share 75:25.

st.2: The All India Services (Conduct) Rules were framed by the UPSC.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the AIS (Conduct) Rules, 1968 were framed by the Central Government under the All India Services Act, 1951, not by the UPSC.

st.2: It is a quasi-judicial body.
st.3: It submits its reports to the President.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Law Commission is an advisory body, not quasi-judicial. Statement 3 is wrong: it reports to the Union Ministry of Law and Justice.

st.3: India ratified the ILO Convention on the Rights of the Child on 11 December 1992.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Convention on the Rights of the Child is a UN convention (1989), not an ILO one; it treats persons below 18 as children.

st.2: It submits its annual consolidated report to the Chief Minister.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Lokayukta reports to the Governor, not the Chief Minister.

st.1: Only a court can attach property believed to be proceeds of crime.
st.2: The Enforcement Directorate works under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ED Director can provisionally attach such property without a court. Statement 2 is wrong: the ED is under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.

st.2: The States together have one-third of the vote weight in the Council.
st.4: In Mohit Minerals (May 2022) the Supreme Court held its recommendations binding on the States.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Centre has one-third and the States together two-thirds of the vote weight. Statement 4 is wrong: Mohit Minerals held the recommendations persuasive, not binding.

st.3: It was appointed by the Government of Tamil Nadu.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Sarkaria Commission (1983) was appointed by the Central Government; Tamil Nadu set up the Rajamannar Committee.

st.2: The Governor should be removed only by impeachment by Parliament.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Punchhi Commission suggested impeachment of the Governor by the State Legislature, not by Parliament.

st.2: The 104th Amendment (2019) extended both SC/ST reservation and the nomination of Anglo-Indians till 2030.
st.4: Women's reservation under the 106th Amendment operates immediately, irrespective of census and delimitation.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 104th Amendment extended only SC/ST reservation and ended Anglo-Indian nomination. Statement 4 is wrong: women's reservation starts only after the next census and delimitation.

st.1: The 44th Amendment (1978) froze the State-wise allocation of seats on the 1971 Census till 2000.
st.3: The 87th Amendment (2003) allowed boundaries to be redrawn on the 2001 Census and raised the total number of seats.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the freeze on the 1971 Census was imposed by the 42nd Amendment (1976). Statement 3 is wrong: the 87th Amendment allowed readjustment on the 2001 Census without changing the total number of seats.

st.1: The criteria for declaring an area a Scheduled Area, such as preponderance of tribals and economic backwardness, are laid down in the Fifth Schedule itself.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the criteria are not in the Constitution; they come from commission reports and executive practice.

st.2: The Santhals revere the Niyamgiri Hills as Marang Buru.
st.3: G.S. Ghurye identified political autonomy, recognition of identity and control over resources as the aims of modern tribal movements.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Marang Buru is the Parasnath Hills; Niyamgiri is sacred to the Dongria Kondhs. Statement 3 is wrong: these aims were identified by T.K. Oommen; Ghurye held the assimilationist view.

st.2: The Smart Cities Mission, launched on 25 June 2015 for 100 cities, is run by NITI Aayog.
st.3: The Urban Infrastructure Development Fund announced in Budget 2023-24 is operated through NABARD.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Smart Cities Mission is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Statement 3 is wrong: the UIDF is operated through the National Housing Bank.

st.3: Trading under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is regulated by SEBI.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: trading under the CCTS is regulated by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission, not SEBI.

st.3: Atmanirbhar Bharat was announced in May 2019.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Atmanirbhar Bharat was announced in May 2020, during the COVID-19 lockdown.

st.2: Laxmikanth ranks trade unions as the most powerful pressure groups in India.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Laxmikanth ranks business groups (FICCI, CII, ASSOCHAM) as the most powerful pressure groups.

st.1: The Commerce Minister is a member of the Cabinet Committee on Security.
st.2: The National Security Adviser chairs the National Security Council, set up in 1998.
st.3: The Committee on External Affairs is serviced by the Rajya Sabha.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the CCS has the PM and the Home, Defence, Finance and External Affairs Ministers. Statement 2 is wrong: the NSC is chaired by the PM; the NSA is its secretary. Statement 3 is wrong: the Committee on External Affairs is serviced by the Lok Sabha.

st.2: The Centre's capital expenditure in the Union Budget 2026-27 is lower than in 2025-26.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: capital expenditure was raised to ₹12.2 lakh crore in Budget 2026-27, higher than the previous year.

st.3: India accounts for about 17.5% of the world's population.

x: All three statements are correct: 1961-71 had the highest decadal growth (24.80%), 1971-81 the highest annual exponential growth (2.22%), and India has about 17.5% of the world's population.

st.2: It is implemented by NABARD.
st.3: Its margin money subsidy is a flat 25% for all beneficiaries.
st.4: The maximum project cost is ₹20 lakh for a manufacturing unit and ₹50 lakh for a service unit.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: PMEGP is implemented by the KVIC. Statement 3 is wrong: the subsidy varies from 15% to 35% by category and area. Statement 4 is wrong: the limits are reversed: ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for services.

st.2: The slogan of the Ujjwala Yojana is 'Give It Up'.
st.3: Under Ujjwala, the LPG connection is given in the name of the male head of the household.
st.4: PAHAL, the DBT for LPG subsidy, was launched nationally on 15 November 2014.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Ujjwala's slogan is 'Swachh Indhan Behtar Jeevan'; 'Give It Up' was the subsidy-surrender campaign. Statement 3 is wrong: the connection is given in the name of an adult woman. Statement 4 is wrong: PAHAL began in 54 districts on 15 November 2014 and went national on 1 January 2015.

st.1: DWCRA (1982-83) was started as a sub-scheme of TRYSEM.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: DWCRA was a sub-scheme of the IRDP, not TRYSEM.

st.3: Intermediate goods are included in national income so that all production is captured.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: intermediate goods are excluded from national income to avoid double counting.

st.2: The first inflation print of the new CPI series, for January 2026, was released by the RBI.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: CPI data are released by the National Statistics Office (MoSPI), not the RBI.

st.2: The four Labour Codes are on the State List.
st.4: India's social-protection coverage rose from 19% (2015) to 64.3% (2025), ahead of China.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: labour is a Concurrent List subject; the four Codes merged 29 central laws. Statement 4 is wrong: India is second only to China, not ahead of it.

st.4: Cultivators rose from 118.8 million (2001) to 127.3 million (2011).

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the direction is reversed: cultivators fell from 127.3 million (2001) to 118.8 million (2011).

st.1: Human development means enlarging people's choices, and income is the end of development.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: in human development income is only a means; people's well-being is the end.

st.1: The Uniform Recall Period uses different recall periods for different items.
st.3: The Modified Mixed Recall Period was used by the Tendulkar Committee.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: URP uses the same 30-day recall for all items. Statement 3 is wrong: MMRP (first used in 2009-10) was used by the Rangarajan Committee; Tendulkar used MRP.
Both statements are correct: the National MPI has three equally weighted dimensions (health, education, standard of living) and uses NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 data.

st.2: Persons with post-secondary education have a higher poverty ratio than those with no formal education.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the relation is reversed: 35.1% of those with no formal education are poor against 14.9% of those with post-secondary education.

st.1: The World Bank Stand-By Arrangement approved on 31 October 1991 was for SDR 1,656 million over 20 months.
st.3: India's 1978 demonetisation was carried out by the Indira Gandhi government.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Stand-By Arrangement was the IMF's, not the World Bank's. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1978 demonetisation was done by Morarji Desai's Janata government.

st.1: It made grants, not tax devolution, the main route of transfers.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Fourteenth Finance Commission made tax devolution (42%), not grants, the main route.

st.1: Andhra Pradesh sought the Finance Commission's help in 2023 to set up a State Institution for Transformation.
st.3: Visakhapatnam is a pilot city under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs' City and Regional Growth Hubs (G-HUB) initiative.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP sought NITI Aayog's help for the State Institution for Transformation. Statement 3 is wrong: G-HUB is NITI Aayog's initiative (four pilot cities), not MoHUA's.

st.2: The money multiplier rises.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a higher CRR lowers the money multiplier.

st.2: It was incorporated as a Section 8 company under the Companies Act, 1956.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NPCI was incorporated under Section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956 (now Section 8 of the 2013 Act).

st.1: Payments banks can accept fixed deposits of up to ₹2 lakh per customer.
st.2: Payments banks can issue both debit and credit cards.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: payments banks take only demand deposits (up to ₹2 lakh), not fixed deposits. Statement 2 is wrong: they cannot lend, so they issue debit cards but no credit cards. Statement 3 is wrong: small finance banks must keep 50% (not 75%) of loans in loans of up to ₹25 lakh.

st.2: Its nodal department is the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: PMJDY's nodal department is the Department of Financial Services.

st.2: The CRR has a statutory floor of 3% and a ceiling of 20%.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2006 amendment removed the CRR floor and ceiling.

st.2: Lower risk weights are used to cool hot sectors.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: hot sectors are cooled with higher risk weights, not lower ones.

st.2: Dual control by the RBI and SEBI weakened its oversight.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the dual control was by the RBI and the State Registrars of Cooperative Societies, not SEBI.

st.2: A statutory Public Debt Management Agency was set up after the 2015-16 Budget.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the statutory PDMA was never set up; only a non-statutory cell exists.

st.3: From 2006-07 the RBI may freely subscribe to primary issues of G-Secs.
st.4: Use of Ways and Means Advances beyond the permitted limit is called a monetised deficit.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: under the FRBM Act the RBI is barred from primary G-Sec issues from 2006-07, except under the escape clause. Statement 4 is wrong: WMA use beyond the limit is an overdraft; the monetised deficit is the RBI's net credit to the government.

st.1: The impact of a tax is on the person who finally bears it.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: impact falls on the person who first pays the tax; the final burden is its incidence.

st.1: Estate duty was introduced in 1953 and is still in force.
st.3: Gift tax is still in force.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: estate duty was abolished in 1985. Statement 3 is wrong: gift tax was abolished in 1998.

st.2: Faceless appeals were launched by the GST Council in September 2020.
st.4: e-Sahyog is a scheme for faceless appeals.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: faceless appeals are an income-tax (CBDT) reform, not a GST Council one. Statement 4 is wrong: e-Sahyog is an online check of mismatches, not faceless appeals.

st.2: Nil-rated supplies allow input tax credit.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: nil-rated supplies do not allow input tax credit; only zero-rated supplies do.

st.1: India ranked 3rd in the Global South for trade-partner diversity in the WTO's World Trade Report 2025.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ranking (India 3rd, after China and the UAE) is from UNCTAD's Trade and Development Report 2025, not a WTO report.

st.2: The average holding rose to 1.08 ha in 2015-16 from 1.15 ha in 2010-11.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the average holding fell, from 1.15 ha (2010-11) to 1.08 ha (2015-16).

st.2: The Global Hunger Index is published by the FAO.
st.3: The SOFI report is led by the FAO; SOFI 2026 found that Asia still has more hungry people than Africa.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the GHI is published by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe. Statement 3 is wrong: SOFI 2026 found that Africa (about 309 million) has overtaken Asia.

st.2: It narrowed regional disparity among States.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Green Revolution widened regional disparity, favouring Punjab, Haryana and western UP.

st.1: PSL covers agriculture, micro and small enterprises, weaker sections and renewable energy, but not education or housing.
st.3: The Narasimham Committee (1991) proposed widening the PSL target to 50%.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: education and housing are also priority sectors. Statement 3 is wrong: the Narasimham Committee proposed cutting the PSL target to 10%, not widening it.

st.1: The Department of Public Enterprises brings out the Public Enterprises Survey on the advice of the Committee on Public Undertakings.
st.3: The Public Enterprises Survey also covers public sector banks and insurers.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Survey is brought out on the advice of the Estimates Committee. Statement 3 is wrong: it leaves out banks, insurers and departmental undertakings.

st.2: It gives a capital subsidy of 45% to general MSMEs.
st.4: The AP Maritime Policy aims to handle 20% of India's port cargo and have one port in the world's top 20 by 2030.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: general MSMEs get 25%; 45% is for special categories. Statement 4 is wrong: the target year for a top-20 port and a 20% cargo share is 2047, not 2030.

st.1: PLI-Auto is run by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: PLI-Auto is run by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (and needs at least 50% domestic value addition).

st.1: The Jan Vishwas 2.0 Bill repeals 16 Acts.
st.2: It decriminalises all 355 provisions it amends.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Bill amends 16 Acts; it does not repeal them. Statement 2 is wrong: it decriminalises 288 of the 355 provisions, not all.

st.2: Only the Central or a State Government can set up an SEZ.
st.4: Section 10AA benefits are available to new units without any sunset date.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: private developers can also set up SEZs. Statement 4 is wrong: Section 10AA had a sunset; only units operational by 30 June 2020 get it.

st.3: Forestry was the fastest-growing agricultural sub-sector in 2024-25 (14.99%).

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the fastest-growing agricultural sub-sector in 2024-25 was crops (14.99%), not forestry.

st.1: India's foodgrain output has been higher than its horticulture output since 2012-13.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the relation is reversed: horticulture output has exceeded foodgrain output since 2012-13.

st.1: Just after bifurcation it was about 60% services-dependent, with manufacturing about 10.5% of GSDP.
st.2: The '10.5% of GSDP' figure refers to the whole industry sector including mining, construction and utilities.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: residual AP was about 60% agriculture-dependent, not services-dependent. Statement 2 is wrong: the 10.5% figure is manufacturing only, not the whole industry sector.

st.3: During 2014-24 capex of all States was higher than their revenue expenditure.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: State capital expenditure has stayed a small share of total spending, far below revenue expenditure.

st.2: Section 94(4) provides for special financial support for the Raj Bhavan, High Court and Secretariat of the new capital.
st.3: The Capital City Advisory Committee of the AP government was chaired by G.N. Rao.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: special financial support for the capital's buildings is Section 94(3); 94(4) is about denotifying degraded forest land. Statement 3 is wrong: the Capital City Advisory Committee was chaired by P. Narayana; G.N. Rao led a later committee.

st.1: Rayalaseema now has 8 districts, including Nellore.
st.3: The Sri Bagh Pact (16 November 1937) was signed at Kurnool.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Nellore is a coastal district, not one of Rayalaseema's eight. Statement 3 is wrong: the Sri Bagh Pact was signed at Sri Bagh, K. Nageswara Rao's house in Madras.

st.1: It won the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity alone, without sharing it.
st.2: The Food Planet Prize, for which APCNF was the first Indian finalist in 2026, is awarded from Norway.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: APCNF shared the Gulbenkian Prize (2024). Statement 2 is wrong: the Food Planet Prize is given by Sweden's Curt Bergfors Foundation.

st.3: It named fisheries and sericulture as growth engines.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the December 2018 White Paper named livestock and horticulture as the growth engines.
All three statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh ranks first in oil-palm area, has about 48% of India's oil-palm area, and leads in productivity too.

st.1: The AP MedTech Zone (AMTZ) was set up at Tirupati in 2016.
st.2: The MAS (Sri Lanka) apparel park under the 2006 MoU is in Guntur.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AMTZ is at Visakhapatnam, not Tirupati. Statement 2 is wrong: the MAS apparel park is in Nellore, not Guntur.

st.1: SEEPZ at Santacruz, Mumbai, was Asia's first Export Processing Zone.
st.3: Noida, set up in 1997, was the first private-sector EPZ.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Asia's first EPZ was Kandla (1965); SEEPZ came in 1973. Statement 3 is wrong: the first private-sector EPZ was Surat (1997), not Noida.

st.1: An SEZ can be developed only by the Central Government or a State Government.
st.3: 100% FDI in SEZs is allowed only through the government approval route.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: private developers can also set up SEZs. Statement 3 is wrong: 100% FDI is allowed under the automatic route for most manufacturing in SEZs.

st.2: The Government of India shall provide rapid rail and road connectivity from the new capital of Andhra Pradesh to Hyderabad within one year of the appointed day.
st.3: Industrial parks of the AP Industrial Corridor Development Authority are notified under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Schedule only says the Centre shall 'take steps' for this connectivity, with no deadline. Statement 3 is wrong: the parks are notified under Section 3 of the AP-ICDA Act, 2017, not the Reorganisation Act.

st.2: APIIC is the nodal agency of that policy.
st.4: Paradip, a national green hydrogen hub, is in Andhra Pradesh.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the nodal agency of the Green Hydrogen Policy is NREDCAP, not APIIC. Statement 4 is wrong: Paradip is in Odisha.

st.2: Startup India Yatra searches for entrepreneurial talent in villages.
st.3: MAARG is a national mentorship platform only for artificial-intelligence start-ups.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Startup India Yatra looks for talent in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, not villages. Statement 3 is wrong: MAARG covers start-ups of all sectors, not only AI.

st.1: Sunspots are hotter and brighter than the surrounding photosphere.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: sunspots are cooler and darker than the surrounding photosphere.

st.2: On the December solstice, the noon Sun at the Tropic of Cancer stands at an altitude of 43°.

x: All three statements are correct: the Tropics are 47° apart, on the December solstice the noon Sun at the Tropic of Cancer is 47° from the zenith and so 43° above the horizon, and the torrid zone lies between the Tropics.

st.3: A place at 35°W has a local time ahead of a place at 25°E.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the place at 25°E, lying to the east, is ahead, by 4 hours (60° x 4 minutes).

st.2: Samoa moved to the American side of the Date Line in 2011.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: in 2011 Samoa moved to the western (Asian/Australian) side of the Date Line, skipping 30 December.

st.2: The theme for 2026 was 'Yoga for One Earth, One Health'.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 'Yoga for One Earth, One Health' was the 2025 theme; 2026's was 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing'.

st.2: Rift valleys are formed by tension (pulling apart) of the crust.
st.4: The Sierra Nevada is a graben.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: horsts form block mountains and grabens rift valleys, rift valleys form under tension, and Death Valley is a rift valley. Statement 4 is wrong: the Sierra Nevada is a block mountain (an uplifted fault block), not a graben.

st.3: Under the Supreme Court's November 2025 definition, an Aravalli hill's height is measured above mean sea level.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the definition measures height above local relief (at least 100 m), not above mean sea level.

st.3: Stromboli lies in the East African Rift belt.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Stromboli lies in the Mediterranean belt, not the East African Rift.

st.2: Calcareous ooze is made of the calcium carbonate shells of organisms such as foraminifera.

x: All three statements are correct: terrigenous deposits get finer away from the shore, calcareous ooze is made of calcium carbonate shells (silica skeletons of diatoms form siliceous ooze), and red clay is most widespread, chiefly in the deep Pacific.

st.3: Lake Tanganyika lies wholly south of the Equator.
st.4: By area, Lake Michigan is larger than Lake Victoria.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Baikal is the deepest and oldest lake, Victoria is the second-largest freshwater lake and source of the White Nile, and Tanganyika lies wholly south of the Equator. Statement 4 is wrong: Lake Victoria is larger than Lake Michigan.

st.1: The Caspian is the largest freshwater lake by area.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Caspian is a saltwater lake; the largest freshwater lake by area is Superior.

st.3: The Gobi is a hot tropical desert.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Gobi is a cold, mid-latitude desert, not a hot tropical one.

st.4: Water vapour decreases with height and from the equator towards the poles.

x: All four statements are correct: water vapour is the most abundant greenhouse gas, methane and nitrous oxide are greenhouse gases while argon and helium are not, vapour can reach 4% in the wet tropics, and it decreases with height and towards the poles.

st.3: It passes through Tripura.

x: All four statements are correct: the Tropic of Cancer crosses eight States (Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram), including Tripura, and AP lies wholly south of it; it does not touch Odisha.
Both statements are correct: the Ten Degree Channel separates the Andamans from the Nicobars, and the Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives.

st.2: 1,60,205 sq km is the area of Andhra Pradesh after the seven Khammam mandals were added.
st.4: Rayalaseema is larger in area than Coastal Andhra.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 1,60,205 sq km was the area before the seven mandals were added; after, it is 1,62,970 sq km. Statement 4 is wrong: Coastal Andhra is larger than Rayalaseema.

st.1: The Krishna delta spreads mainly over Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla districts.

x: All four statements are correct: the Krishna delta covers Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla (Kakinada and Konaseema are Godavari delta), the Penna meets the sea at Utukuru, Konaseema is known for coconut and banana, and Yanam lies in the Godavari delta.

st.1: The Gandikota reservoir is on the Tungabhadra in Kadapa district.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Gandikota reservoir in Kadapa district is on the Penna, not the Tungabhadra.

st.2: The Hindon joins the Yamuna on its right bank.
st.4: The Betwa joins the Chambal.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Hindon is a left-bank tributary of the Yamuna. Statement 4 is wrong: the Betwa joins the Yamuna, not the Chambal.

st.1: The Godavari, about 1,465 km long, is the longest river of Peninsular India.

x: All three statements are correct: the Godavari (about 1,465 km) is the longest Peninsular river, rises at Trimbakeshwar, Nashik, and its Gautami branch meets the sea near Yanam and the Vasishta at Antarvedi.

st.1: Unclassed Forests make up the largest share of the notified forest area.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Reserved Forests (85.8%) form the largest share; Unclassed Forests are only about 0.6%.

st.2: Weak governance and poor coordination are examples of institutional (systemic) vulnerability.

x: All four statements are correct: mangrove loss is environmental vulnerability, weak governance is institutional vulnerability, crop insurance reduces vulnerability, and risk falls as coping capacity rises.

st.2: Visakhapatnam was the world's leading producer of manganese until 1947.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Visakhapatnam was the world's leading manganese producer only until 1929.

st.2: Before the Green Revolution India imported wheat under the Marshall Plan.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India imported wheat under the US PL-480 programme; the Marshall Plan was for Europe.

st.3: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by the National Dairy Research Institute.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Operation Flood was launched by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), not the NDRI.

st.3: With freight loading of 1,617 million tonnes in 2024-25 it is the world's largest freight railway.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: with 1,617 MT Indian Railways is the world's second-largest freight railway, not the largest.

st.3: Krishnapatnam Port gives the State the highest revenue share, 22% of its gross income.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the highest government revenue share (22% of gross income) comes from the Kakinada Deep Water Port, not Krishnapatnam.

st.2: Tamil Nadu has the longest coastline, followed by Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh.
st.4: Ports carry about 68% of India's trade by volume and about 95% by value.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Gujarat has the longest coastline, then Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. Statement 4 is wrong: the shares are reversed: about 95% by volume and 68% by value.

st.2: The broadband satellite GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20) was launched in November 2024 on SpaceX's Falcon 9.

x: Both statements are correct: INSAT-1B (1983) was the first fully operational INSAT, and GSAT-N2 was launched in November 2024 on a SpaceX Falcon 9, not an ISRO rocket.

st.2: Industrial Development Policy 4.0 plans 175+ industrial parks, all of them in Rayalaseema.

st.1: India remained in the Medium human development category.

st.3: Casual labour accounted for 18.9% of employment.

x: All four statements are correct: agriculture had 42.4%, self-employment 55.8% and casual labour 18.9% of employment, and a falling unemployment rate may reflect distress entry into low-productivity work.

st.2: Swarna Andhra Population Management Day is observed on every second Saturday.
st.3: The Chief Minister announced Rs 40,000 for a third child.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Day is observed every fourth Saturday. Statement 3 is wrong: Rs 30,000 was announced for a third child; Rs 40,000 is for a fourth.

st.2: The density of residual AP in 2001 was 252 per sq km.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 252 per sq km was the 1991 density; in 2001 it was 279.

st.2: The border pockets of Kurnool district speak mainly Urdu.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kurnool's border pockets, next to Karnataka, speak mainly Kannada, not Urdu.

st.3: The last cheetahs in India were shot in Gir, Gujarat, in 1947.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the last cheetahs were shot in Koriya (now Chhattisgarh) in 1947, and the species was declared extinct in 1952; Gir is the home of the Asiatic lion.

st.1: Gir in Gujarat is one of India's tiger reserves.
st.4: M-STrIPES is a DNA-based method of counting tigers.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Gir is a lion sanctuary and national park, not a tiger reserve. Statement 4 is wrong: M-STrIPES is an app-based patrolling and monitoring system, not DNA counting.

st.3: Coffee and sugarcane were domesticated in the New World.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: coffee (Ethiopia) and sugarcane (New Guinea/South Asia) are Old World crops.

st.3: The Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI), launched in 2019, has its secretariat in Geneva.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the CDRI secretariat is in New Delhi, not Geneva.

st.3: It subsumed CSIR.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: ANRF subsumed the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB), not CSIR.

st.2: AP DigiVerify runs on a public, permissionless blockchain.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP DigiVerify runs on a permissioned blockchain open only to authorised entities.

st.3: Nano Urea fully replaces conventional urea.
st.4: Nano DAP was notified under the Fertiliser Control Order only for soil application.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Nano Urea only cuts the need for conventional urea; it does not fully replace it. Statement 4 is wrong: Nano DAP (notified 2 March 2023) is for seed treatment and foliar use.

st.3: GSAT-19, India's heaviest launch of 2017, was carried by GSLV-F05.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: GSAT-19 was carried by GSLV Mk III-D1; GSLV-F05 launched INSAT-3DR.

st.2: Its original signals are in the L1 and L2 bands.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NavIC's original signals are in the L5 and S bands (L1 was added later).

st.3: Universal digital literacy and services in Indian languages fall under its vision area 'Governance and services on demand'.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: universal digital literacy and Indian-language services belong to the vision area 'Digital empowerment of citizens'.

st.1: MeeSeva ('At your service') was launched on 4 November 2011 from Visakhapatnam.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: MeeSeva was launched from Chittoor, not Visakhapatnam.

st.3: The SMART governance model and HITEC City IT push of 1995-2004 were led by Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1995-2004 SMART governance and HITEC City push was led by N. Chandrababu Naidu.

st.2: A worm must attach itself to an existing program before it can spread over a network.
st.3: A trojan replicates itself across the network without any user action.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a worm is standalone and spreads without a host program. Statement 3 is wrong: a trojan does not replicate; it poses as useful software and needs the user to run it.

st.2: Projects under the CCPWC scheme are linked to the PM CARES Fund.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: CCPWC projects are funded from the Nirbhaya Fund, not PM CARES.

st.2: Members of the Data Protection Board are appointed by the President on the advice of a collegium headed by the CJI.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Data Protection Board members are appointed by the Central Government.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: village electrification (28 April 2018) was achieved under the DDUGJY; Saubhagya is for household connections.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the India Electric Mobility Index was released by NITI Aayog.

st.2: E20 petrol, mandated from 1 April 2026, contains 20% methanol.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: E20 is petrol with 20% ethanol, not methanol (mandated with a minimum 95 RON).

st.1: Dominant vegetation is a population attribute.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: dominance is a community attribute; population attributes include density, natality, mortality and age structure.

st.2: A grassland forms an ecotone between fresh water and salt water.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the ecotone between fresh and salt water is an estuary; a grassland lies between forest and desert.

st.4: The IUCN Red List, which recorded 784 extinctions in 2014, is published by the WWF.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Red List is published by the IUCN, not the WWF (it recorded 784 extinctions over 500 years).

st.1: Excess use of urea has skewed the NPK ratio of soils mainly in Rajasthan and Gujarat.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: urea overuse has skewed the NPK ratio mainly in Punjab and Haryana.

st.2: Most of these were community titles.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: almost all were individual titles (2,10,828); only 1,822 were community titles.

st.3: The Sub-Mission on Agroforestry is implemented under PM-KISAN.
st.4: The Trees Outside Forests in India (TOFI) programme is run by the MoEFCC with the World Bank.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: SMAF is implemented under PM-RKVY. Statement 4 is wrong: TOFI is run by the MoEFCC with USAID.

st.3: CAMPA funds may be used for private urban housing projects.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: CAMPA funds are for afforestation and forest regeneration, not private housing.

st.2: The Indore method of composting is an anaerobic pit method.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Indore method is aerobic composting with regular turning; the Bangalore method is anaerobic.

st.2: MSE-GIFT is a GST relief scheme for small exporters.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: MSE-GIFT (Green Investment and Financing for Transformation) supports green technology in MSEs, not GST relief.

st.3: Nano DAP was notified in the Fertiliser Control Order before nano urea.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: nano urea came first (2021); Nano DAP was notified later, on 2 March 2023.

st.3: The extra hydrogen ions bind bicarbonate ions, so the carbonate ion concentration rises.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the extra hydrogen ions bind carbonate ions, so carbonate ion concentration falls.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the IPCC Secretariat is at Geneva; Nairobi hosts UNEP.

st.2: Under it, an Annex I party runs an emission-cutting project in another Annex I country.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the CDM is under Article 12; Article 6 provides Joint Implementation. Statement 2 is wrong: CDM projects are run in non-Annex I (developing) countries.

st.3: Its objective is limited to cutting carbon dioxide from fossil fuels.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the UNFCCC aims to stabilise all greenhouse gas concentrations, not only fossil-fuel CO2.

st.1: The CDRI is a treaty-based intergovernmental organisation.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the CDRI is a voluntary multi-stakeholder partnership, not a treaty-based body.

st.3: In increasing order of severity, drug resistance is graded XDR, MDR, TDR.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the order is MDR, XDR, TDR.

st.3: Translational research is curiosity-driven.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: translational research is application-driven; basic research is curiosity-driven.

st.4: A well-tested theory finally becomes a law.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: a theory never turns into a law; a law describes what happens, a theory explains why.

st.2: The elementary charge is 1.6 × 10^19 C.
st.3: A light year is a unit of time.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the elementary charge is 1.6 × 10^-19 C. Statement 3 is wrong: a light year is a unit of distance.

st.2: 100% FDI is allowed in the inventory model.
st.4: ONDC is a payment gateway regulated by RBI.

st.2: India is not among its priority countries.
st.3: It supports Nationally Determined Contributions under the Kyoto Protocol.

st.3: The presidency is run from the permanent BRICS Secretariat in New Delhi.

st.3: NPCI International set up a payment linkage with Malaysia's Maybank.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: NPCI International's linkage is with PayNet, Malaysia's payment network, not Maybank.

st.2: Brazil holds the G20 presidency after South Africa, in 2026.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the USA holds the G20 presidency in 2026; Brazil held it in 2024.

st.3: COP32 (2027) will be held at Nairobi.
st.4: After India withdrew its bid for COP33, Japan is the only other contender.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: COP32 will be at Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Statement 4 is wrong: South Korea is the only other COP33 contender.

st.4: Its New Delhi Declaration is legally binding on the signatories.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the New Delhi Declaration is a voluntary, non-binding statement.

st.2: With 192 States Parties it is UNESCO's most widely ratified convention.

st.3: Iraq is one of its members.

st.3: India has signed but not ratified the NPT.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India has never signed the NPT.

st.2: The EU is India's first FTA partner in Europe.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the India-EFTA TEPA (2024) came first; the EU is India's 22nd FTA partner.

st.3: India signed the Convention on Supplementary Compensation in 2010 but has not ratified it.

st.3: India and New Zealand established diplomatic relations in 1947.

st.4: DUSTLIK is the India-Kazakhstan army exercise.
